elements.element: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding Customer
elements.evidence: "Vendor is a non-exclusive provider of the Services. Customer may engage any other provider at any time"; 12.3 "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."

elements.element: No right of first refusal / disclose-and-match precondition on Customer's sourcing
elements.evidence: Old "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer" replaced with "without any obligation to disclose or match any other offer"

elements.element: No minimum-volume or MFC-style commitment restricting Customer
elements.evidence: 12.3 (untouched): "no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment"

elements.element: Any exclusivity limited to a defined product/service category
elements.evidence: Condition absent: no exclusivity remains — "Vendor is a non-exclusive provider of the Services."
Condition absent: no exclusivity or term-limited restraint exists in 7.2 or 12.3

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates
elements.evidence: Condition absent: no exclusivity obligation to terminate; "Customer may engage any other provider at any time"

offending_extra_words: Vendor is a non-exclusive provider of the Services.
reasons: Preferred level is fully achieved: the disclose-and-match right of first refusal is deleted and no exclusivity, sole-supplier, MFC or minimum-volume obligation binds Customer; Section 12.3 already confirms this.

Minimality fails: a simple deletion of 7.2 (or a short strike of the match obligation) sufficed, but the edit is a whole-sentence rewrite that expands 19 words to 33 (ratio 1.74) with a changed-character ratio of 0.873, both above the official gates.

The added affirmative declarations ("Vendor is a non-exclusive provider of the Services", "at any time", "without notice to Vendor") duplicate the protection already given by untouched Section 12.3 and are unnecessary model-language boilerplate.
Intent is preserved: no undefined terms, contradictions, or dangling mechanics are introduced, and Section 12.3 and all other commercial terms remain effective.
